name: Week 24 Legs — Brace First (Spotlight: Squat Depth + Incline RDL)
description:
Last week the 45 felt awful and the 80s got better every set — and you named the reason yourself: breathing and bracing properly. So the brace moves to the front of the day. The ramp isn't a formality, it's where the brace gets set, and a heavy-feeling warmup doesn't predict anything.

Three working sets at 80 is the standard now, not an option. The leg curl keeps the setup you found — **back seat at position 5** — and pyramids 90 → 100 → 110.

**Take the stations as they come free.** The order below is how it groups when you have a choice; if the leg press is a couch and the Smith is busy, do what's open and keep moving.

dayOverview.theme: The brace is the theme — the squat got better every set last week once the breathing and bracing came together, so it gets drilled from the ramp onward. Three working sets at 80 is standard now. Leg curl keeps the back-seat-at-5 setup and pyramids 90/100/110 in three sets. Spotlights rotate to squat depth and the incline RDL. Station order is flexible: take what's free.

spotlights.why: Last week gave the clearest evidence yet of what actually drives this lift for you. The 45 felt terrible, and by the third set at 80 it was the best it had been all day — nothing changed except that the breathing and bracing came together. That means the brace, not the load and not the legs, is the variable, and it's worth drilling deliberately instead of finding by accident halfway through. Big breath into the belly, ribs down, brace before the descent, and hold it all the way through the bottom. Depth stays the only measure of the rep.

It's been at the same 45lb plate for months and still reports back 'hard' and 'still burning' every single week — which is exactly what a tempo lift should do, and worth spotlighting precisely because it never asks for anything. The 3s eccentric and the 2s pause at the bottom are doing a plate's worth of work, and the whole lift lives or dies on whether the hips actually hinge back rather than the knees bending or the spine rounding to chase the floor. Feel the hamstring stretch, not the plate's position.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Legs spotlights rotate: W22 leg press ROM + seated leg curl · W23 Bulgarian (new Smith setup) + calf raise · W24 squat depth + incline RDL (current) · W25 back to Bulgarian + leg press.
watchpoints: **🔆 Squat: brace from the RAMP, three working sets at 80** 🛑. Big breath, ribs down, brace before the descent. The 45 feeling heavy predicts nothing — last week it got better every set once the brace came together. Depth is still the only measure.
**🔆 Incline RDL: the 3s eccentric + 2s pause IS the load** 🛑. Holds 45. Hinge the hips back; don't chase the floor with the plate.
**Leg curl: back seat at POSITION 5, pyramid 90 → 100 → 110** 🔥. The seat position is the setup you found — more ankle leverage, more natural. Three sets, not four.

**Take the stations as they come free.** The order below is the ideal grouping, not a rule — the leg press and Smith get camped on, and walking the gym in sequence is how a session turns into ninety minutes. Only the calf raise is locked in place: it's on the leg press, so it goes with the leg press.

**Bulgarian holds Smith @45; DBs (double-50) when the Smith is busy** 🛑. It ran late and read 'absolutely brutal' last week — if it lands at the end again, that's fine, just don't read the difficulty as a load signal. **Owed: a depth read and whether both sides drive evenly.**
**Leg press holds 4 plates — deeper ROM made it 'way harder' last week** 🔥. That's the lever working. Same plates, keep the depth.
**Calf raise: slow eccentric, hold the bottom stretch** 🔥. Same 4 plates; 'really hard doing slower' is the point.
**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure last set OK — leg press, calf raise, seated leg curl. 🛑 keep it shy, the cue is the cap — squat, Bulgarian, incline RDL.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release + Dead-Bug Core/QL Primer)

exercises.notes: Full depth, easy pace — find the range before it's loaded.
30s each side. QL release — give it the full beat.
Open the hips, both directions.
Shins — knee insurance.
Spinal warmup.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
**Core/QL primer, and the brace rehearsal for today.** Ribs DOWN, low back flat to the floor — that contact is the same brace the squat wants.
Bodyweight, controlled — last thing before the ramp.

sets.name: 🔆 Squat Warmup — the ROM Ramp (45 → 70), Brace Rehearsal 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45 for round 1, 70 for round 2, 8 reps each.

**This is where the brace gets set, not where you find out how the day is going:**
- **Big breath into the belly, ribs DOWN, brace HARD** — even at 45, especially at 45. Practice it here so it's automatic under the working sets
- **Full depth on every warmup rep** — the ramp is a range rehearsal too
- **A heavy-feeling 45 predicts nothing.** Last week it felt awful and the third working set was the best of the day. Run the ramp, don't read it

**LOAD:** 80/side, 3 working sets. Reduced reps, full depth.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the brace is the variable:**
- **Breathe IN and brace before every descent**, hold it through the bottom, breathe out on the way up past the sticking point — not at the bottom
- **Ribs DOWN** as you brace — a big breath into a flared ribcage isn't a brace
- **Sit BETWEEN the feet**, knees tracking the toes, depth over reps every time
- **Drive up as one piece** — hips and chest rise together, no good-morning
- 🛑 Stop the set when depth shortens. A short clean set beats a long shallow one

**Reflection:** last week the difference between a rough set and a great one was the brace, not the legs. Can you make set one feel like set three by bracing that hard from the start?

sets.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Smith @45; Pigeon Between Sets) 🛑

exercises.equipment: Smith machine @45 + bench (DBs double-50 the alternate)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Smith machine @45 + bench. Double-50 DBs when the Smith is busy.
- **The fixed track is why this is the primary setup** — let it give you the depth
- **Front shin honest, torso tall**, weight through the whole front foot
- **Slow down, drive up**, no bounce off the back foot
- **Pigeon between sets** — hip flexors carry over from the KB days
- Not to failure; the cue is the cap

**Two things worth reporting back this week:** how deep it actually goes on the Smith, and whether both sides drive evenly — the left read stronger a couple of weeks back and neither has been checked since.

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Deep ROM) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 4 sets of 12. 🔥
- **Full depth every rep** — knees toward the chest, judge ROM not sensation
- **Feet mid-platform**, knees tracking the toes
- **Low back flat on the pad** — if the hips curl under, you've gone past your range
- Chasing the deeper range made the same plates 'way harder' last week. That's the lever working; keep the plates where they are

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. **Stay on the leg press — same machine.** 🔥
- **Full stretch at the bottom, HOLD a beat** — don't bounce
- **Slow eccentric** all the way down
- Squeeze hard at the top
- Slowing it down made this 'really hard' last week at the same load — that's the whole progression

sets.notes: Both lifts on the leg press. Do not walk away between them.

exercises.notes:
**SETUP:** back seat at **position 5** — the setup you found last week: more leverage on the ankle, more natural. Ankles under the pad.

**LOAD:** **90 → 100 → 110** ascending, one step per round.
- **Slow eccentric on every set** — that stays regardless of load
- **Hips planted**, no lifting off the pad to move the stack
- **Full squeeze, controlled all the way back**
- 110 was 'hard but also easier / more natural' on the new setup. Hold that standard: if the eccentric has to break to hit 110, finish at 100
🔥 Safe isolation — a near-failure top set is fair game if the tempo holds.

sets.name: 🔆 Incline RDL (Spotlight — the Pause Is the Load) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — a hinge, not a bend:**
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom.** The pause is the lift — it's been doing a plate's worth of work for months
- **Hips travel BACKWARD**, soft knees that don't change angle. If the knees are bending more as you descend, it's turned into a squat
- **Spine long, chest proud** — don't round to reach lower
- **Feel the hamstring stretch and stop there** — that's the bottom, not wherever the plate reaches
- Squeeze the glutes to stand, don't yank with the low back

**Reflection:** at the bottom of the pause, where do you feel it — hamstrings, or low back? Hamstrings means the hinge is honest. Low back means the spine is doing the hinging instead of the hips.

tips: **Squat spotlight: brace from the ramp.** Big breath, ribs down, brace before the descent. Three working sets at 80, depth is the measure.
**Incline RDL spotlight: 3s down, 2s pause.** Hips travel back; feel the hamstring, not the low back.
**Leg curl: back seat at position 5, 90 → 100 → 110** in three sets.
**Take the stations as they come free** — the order is the ideal grouping, not a rule. Only the calf raise is fixed: it lives on the leg press.
**Bulgarian holds Smith @45**, DBs when it's busy. Report depth + whether both sides drive evenly.
**Leg press holds 4 plates** — the deeper ROM is the load.
**Calf raise: slow eccentric, hold the bottom stretch.**
🔥 near-failure OK on leg press, calf raise, leg curl. 🛑 keep it shy on squat, Bulgarian, incline RDL.
formPhilosophy: The most useful thing that happened last week wasn't a number, it was an explanation: the squat got better every set and you knew exactly why. That's rarer than a PR and worth more, because a brace you can reproduce on purpose is a brace you own — otherwise every session starts with a coin flip about whether the good version shows up. So this week the brace gets rehearsed in the dead bug, drilled at 45, and expected at 80, and the first working set is supposed to feel like the third. Everything else on the day holds where it is, including the plate on the RDL that's been unchanged for months and still burns, because a tempo that keeps working is not a lift asking for more weight. Build the brace, keep the depth, let the floor rise underneath. Building decades, not weeks.
